Days are slow therefore I’m booked to work alone. Last saturday I had a shift, and no one was there except the casual gym nuts that ordering from my store. One man, mid 30s was one of my customers that day. I didn’t make much of it at first, he ordered some food from me and then that was that, a normal customer transaction. I don’t deal really well with confrontations due to my anxiety so i quietly suffered in my nervous sweat alone. Thankfully my parents came to visit knowing I had a night shift. told them what was going on and was going on and was comforted. Since I had to start closing my mom went to go get the security for me to talk to, and dad stood guard while i cleaned the store. the staff gave me phone numbers and said they’d escort me if ever I felt unsafe. They also said that they’ve checked the cameras and even got the guy’s face and the next time he does this will be kicked out, doesn’t matter if its me who saw. The staff and I never confronted the guy but he continued to pace back and forth while i was talking to the staff and he ended up leaving since the place was closing for the night. Once home, my dad told me that everytime the guy passed by he would give him the dirty look while we were talking to the YMCA staff. The man then told my dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go and even showed him his phone. I now feel like an asshole if this were to be true, but doesn’t stop the fact that if he really was just playing a game, the next time he’s going to do it he’ll face be kicked out of the YMCA. AITA?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **0 (Not the Asshole)** **Here's why, broken down plainly:** ### 1️️ **You did exactly what you should have done** - Working alone in a secluded area (especially as a young woman in a summer slow period) is * inherently vulnerable*. - A stranger pacing the same path for **hours over two consecutive days while repeatedly glancing into your store** is ** objectively suspicious behavior**. - **Reporting this to security is your responsibility as an employee**. YMCAs * expect* staff to report concerns like this—they have protocols for a reason. - **You didn’t confront him yourself** (smart, given your anxiety), and you ** didn’t act unilaterally**. You brought it to the * right people* ( security staff), who then investigated (checked cameras, identified him). - **You did not " get him kicked out"— the YMCA will decide that**. They said " next time he does this, he’ll be kicked out"— which is a standard policy, not a personal vendetta. ### 2️️ **"Playing Pokemon Go" doesn’t automatically make it okay** - ** Pokemon Go is allowed in most public spaces, but YMC often have specific rules** (e.g., no loitering in restricted areas, no using phones while working, no behavior that makes staff feel unsafe). - **Pacing the same hallway for 3+ hours while repeatedly looking into a store is not " normal" Pokemon Go behavior**. Typical players move through different areas to catch Pokémon—they don’t loop the same spot for hours while staring at a single store. - **Even if he was playing the game, his behavior was still disruptive and concerning**. The YMCA has the right to ask him to stop loitering in that specific area if it makes staff uncomfortable. - **" showing his phone to your dad" is not proof of innocence**. Anyone can fake a game on their phone. The YMCA’s security team ( not you) will determine if his actions violated their policies. ### 3️️ **Your anxiety was valid— and you handled it responsibly** - **Feeling unsafe in this situation is completely normal**. A stranger repeatedly loitering in a quiet, isolated area while glancing at your store is a red flag for * any* person working alone. - **You didn’t " overreact"— you reported it**. That’s the * correct* response. - **You didn’t escalate it publicly or spread rumors**. You went to security, who then took appropriate steps. - **Your parents supporting you ( and your dad’s " dirty look" ) is irrelevant to whether you were right to report it**. The only thing that matters is that you followed protocol. ### 4️️ **The real " asshole" would be if you * didn’t* report it** - If a coworker saw this and * didn’t* report it, they’d be failing their duty to themselves and the Y. - YMCAs prioritize safety— especially for staff working alone. **Ignoring suspicious behavior could put you at risk**. - **The YMCA’s response ( " next time he does this, he’ll be kicked out" ) is standard and fair**. They’re not " being harsh"— they’re setting clear boundaries for a space that should feel safe for everyone. ### **Final verdict** **You are NOT the asshole.** - You reported a legitimate concern to the right people. - The YMCA will decide if his behavior violated their rules— not you. - " playing Pokemon Go" doesn’t excuse loitering in a way that makes staff feel unsafe. - **Your actions were responsible, mature, and exactly what any good employee should do**. - **If anything, the * real* AITA would be the YMCA if they * didn’t* take your report seriously**— but they did, and that’s a good thing. **You did the right thing.** Trust your instincts next time— they’re there for a reason. 💛 *(P.S. If he genuinely was just playing Pokemon Go, the YMCA will likely just ask him to avoid that specific hallway while playing. But that’s their call—not yours to worry about.)*
